2. "retreater" => "ivgivzgvi"
3. "chemical" => "xsvnrxzo"

We need to see mapping.

Let's compute Caesar shift possibilities. For each letter, compute shift from input to output (assuming same case). For "photo" -> "kslgl". Let's map letters:

p -> k: p (16) to k (11) shift -5 (or +21). h -> s: h (8) to s (19) shift +11. t -> l: t (20) to l (12) shift -8 (or +18). o -> g: o (15) to g (7) shift -8. So shifts vary, not constant. So not Caesar.

Atbash: Atbash maps a<->z, b<->y, etc. Let's compute Atbash of "photo": p->k (since p (16) maps to k (11) indeed Atbash: a=1->z=26, so mapping: letter position p=16 => 27-16=11 => k. Good. h=8 => 27-8=19 => s. t=20 => 27-20=7 => g (but output is l). Wait Atbash of t is g, but output is l. So not Atbash.

Check "photo" Atbash yields: p->k, h->s, o->l? Wait compute: o=15 => 27-15=12 => l. Actually we need order: "photo": p h o t o? Wait original "photo": letters p h o t o. Output "kslgl": k s l g l. Let's compute Atbash:

p -> k (matches)
h -> s (matches)
o -> l (matches)
t -> g (output g? Actually output 4th char is g, yes "kslgl": positions: k(1) s(2) l(3) g(4) l(5). So t->g matches.
o -> l (matches). So Atbash matches all! Good.

Thus cipher is Atbash.

Check second example: "retreater" => "ivgivzgvi". Let's Atbash each:

Alphabet positions: a=1...z=26. Atbash: new = 27 - old.

r (18) -> i (9) matches first char i.
e (5) -> v (22) matches second v.
t (20) -> g (7) matches third g.
r (18) -> i (9) matches fourth i.
e (5) -> v (22) matches fifth v.
a (1) -> z (26) matches sixth z.
t (20) -> g (7) matches seventh g.
e (5) -> v (22) matches eighth v.
r (18) -> i (9) matches ninth i.

Matches exactly.

Third: "chemical" => "xsvnrxzo". Let's test:

c (3) -> x (24) matches.
h (8) -> s (19) matches.
e (5) -> v (22) matches.
m (13) -> n (14) matches? Wait Atbash of m (13) => 27-13=14 => n. Output third? Actually output "xsvnrxzo": letters: x s v n r x z o. So fourth char is n matches.
i (9) -> r (18) matches fifth r.
c (3) -> x (24) matches sixth x.
a (1) -> z (26) matches seventh z.
l (12) -> o (15) matches eighth o.

All match. So cipher is Atbash.

Thus answer JSON: {"cipher":"atbash"}.
